title: FOMC minutes of the January 25-26, 2028 meeting — the one sub-class D+21 cannot displace, and the family's most settlement-collided release
source: EST: federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/fomccalendars.htm, re-fetched direct 2026-09-09 (HTTP 200, 164,831 bytes, stamp 'Last Update: August 19, 2026'), states the convention verbatim -- 'The minutes of regularly scheduled meetings are released three weeks after the date of the policy decision' -- and its note below the 2027 panel gives the meeting as 'January 25-26, 2028'. 2028-01-26 is a Wednesday (computed from 2028-01-01 being a Saturday) and +21 days is Wednesday 2028-02-16. THE CENSUS IS THIS SESSION'S OWN PARSE AND IT REPLICATES THE FAMILY'S EXACTLY: the live page plus fomchistorical2007.htm ... fomchistorical2020.htm (fourteen pages, HTTP 200 each) cut into meeting blocks at their own boundaries before each block's minutes link was paired to the '(Released ...)' string inside that same block gives 157 releases, decisions 2007-01-31 -> 2026-07-29, 8/year 2007-2025, with a D+21 x143 / D+20 x8 / D+22 x3 / D+23 x1 / D+19 x1 lag histogram and 14 exceptions by meeting month Nov x6, Dec x4, Jun x2, Oct x1 plus the 2020-03-15 unscheduled meeting at D+24. THE JANUARY SUB-CLASS IS PERFECT, AND THE COUNT IS 18 NOT 20: keyed by DECISION DAY -- the key this calendar uses for an FOMC id and the key D+21 is measured from -- there are 18 January-decision meetings 2007-2026 and all 18 released at exactly D+21, every one Wednesday-to-Wednesday. The proposal that seeded this id said 20; the extra two are 2017-02-01 and 2023-02-01, Jan 31-Feb 1 meetings whose DECISION day falls in February. Both also released at D+21 (2017-02-22, 2023-02-22), so the claim survives under either definition -- but neither is this event's shape, since the 2028 decision is 2028-01-26. AND THE PERFECTION IS STRUCTURAL, NOT LUCK: the only Board of Governors closure near a January-class release is Washington's Birthday, always the third Monday of February; the release is always a Wednesday. A Wednesday is never 0 or 1 day from a Monday, so the gap is quantised to exactly {+2, -5} across all 18 historical cases and can never enter the |gap| <= 1 band where fomc-minutes-2027-12-29.md measured 4 displacements in 5. 2028-02-16 is a -5 case: Washington's Birthday 2028 is Monday 2028-02-21 on TWO primaries fetched today, federalreserve.gov/aboutthefed/k8.htm (HTTP 200, 82,205 bytes, its 2028 column reads 'Washington's Birthday ... February 21') and nyse.com/markets/hours-calendars (HTTP 200 after 302, 109,180 bytes, its 2028 column reads 'Washington's Birthday | Monday, February 21'). 2022 is the exact structural twin: 2022-01-01 and 2028-01-01 are both Saturdays, the 2022 meeting was January 25-26, and its minutes released Wednesday 2022-02-16 at the same -5 gap -- the same date pair, six years earlier. Filed estimate on two counts, neither of them date doubt: the meeting it minutes is itself estimate (the same page: 'Each meeting date is tentative until confirmed at the meeting immediately preceding it', which for this one is the December 2027 meeting), and this lane does not self-confirm an event it discovered in-sweep. Written by the fomc-minutes-2028-02-16 initial research after reading the sole prior proposal, proposals/fomc-minutes-2028-02-16.from-fomc-2028-01-26.json, which is now inert. Checked 2026-09-09
notes: READ IT, DO NOT TRADE IT -- the family's settled posture, and this lane adds the reason the January class only LOOKS special. Nine sibling ledgers have refused this class on the index and on implied vol; nothing here reopens that. THE DISTINCTIVE FACT IS A COLLISION, MEASURED NOT ASSERTED: 2028-02-16 is also the predicted February 2028 VIX settlement Wednesday (30 days before the third Friday of March 2028, 2028-03-17), and the January minutes class is the family's most settlement-collided sub-class by a wide margin -- 13 of 18 historical January-class releases (72.2%) landed on VIX settlement day against 50 of 157 (31.8%) family-wide, because both anchors are Wednesdays inside a narrow February band. That matters because fomc-minutes-2027-11-17.md's live statistic IS the settlement split, and this session replicated it independently to the release count: 50 on-settlement releases run 50.0% VIX-down (P = 0.570 vs a 54.4% universe) against 107 off-settlement at 71.0% (P = 0.0005), split P = 0.0014. THE JANUARY CLASS DOES NOT REFUTE IT AND DOES NOT SUPPORT IT -- at n = 13 its on-settlement half prints 69.2% VIX-down, P = 0.266 against the family's on-settlement pool, simply underpowered. THE RESOLUTION IS THAT NOTHING IS LEFT FOR THE RELEASE: matched on BOTH of the things that actually vary -- the calendar window (Feb 15-21, the class's exact realized span, chosen a priori) and settlement status -- the 18 January-class releases are a perfect null against the 15 comparable sessions, P = 1.000 on VIX-down and P = 0.914 on mean |S&P|. The class's apparent calm (mean |S&P| 0.470% against a 0.798% universe) is mid-February, not the minutes. Universe: 4,949 sessions 2007-01-04 -> 2026-09-04, anchored SPX 7,718.60 / VIX 14.53, the same anchors nine siblings record. NOTHING TRADEABLE IS CLAIMED. symbols is empty, no house playbook (S1/S2/E1/S3/S4 + G1) is rates- or settlement-keyed, and the impact tier is inherited rather than measured: medium matches every other fomc-minutes-* entry. The one thing worth reading these minutes FOR is institutional and is named in the parent ledger fomc-2028-01-26.md: January is the Committee's annual organizational meeting, so its minutes carry the 2028 voter rotation (New York, Cleveland, Boston, St. Louis, Kansas City) and the annual review of the Statement on Longer-Run Goals -- content that ledger already measured as worth nothing on the tape (permutation P = 0.9991). Estimate widens caution and licenses no entry.
